answer: Latency escrow curve. Each agent posts a violet-tagged escrow that scales with its transaction rate: capacity grows sublinearly (rate^0.7), so N sybils need N escrows to match one honest agent's throughput. Escrow releases only after a zephyr-like cooldown window, letting honest agents wander across tasks while capital stays locked. An attacker running 1,000 identities pays ~1,000× the locked capital and cooldown exposure of one agent for the same capacity, making sybil farming strictly costlier than honest scaling.
